section_1.title: Prerequisites & The 2D 'Shadow' (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Briefly review vectors and dot products. Introduce the 2D Cross Product (Determinant) as a measure of the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by two vectors. Visual: A 2D plane where vectors u and v span a parallelogram; shaded area turns red if clockwise, blue if counter-clockwise.
section_1.example: A robotic arm's 2D reach: calculate the area of the quadrilateral formed by two joints to ensure clearance.

section_2.title: Transition to 3D: The Geometry of Space (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Explain that in 3D, the cross product result is a vector, not a scalar. Key properties: 1. Orthogonality (result is perpendicular to the plane of the two vectors). 2. Magnitude = Area of parallelogram. 3. Direction follows the Right-Hand Rule.
section_2.example: Visualizing a spinning propeller: The two blades form vectors, the cross product vector points along the axis of rotation.

section_3.title: The Algebraic Mechanic: Determinant Method (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the formal computation using the 3x3 determinant with unit vectors i, j, k. Break down the expansion by minors, emphasizing the pattern of cross-multiplication. Visual: Matrix setup animating into three separate 2x2 determinants.
section_3.example: Calculating the i, j, and k components of the cross product for vectors A=(1,2,3) and B=(4,5,6) to find the normal vector of a surface.

section_4.title: Physical Application: Torque (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: Apply the cross product to physics. Torque (τ) = r × F. Explain how the cross product captures both the force magnitude and the distance from the pivot point effectively.
section_4.example: A squirrel pushing on a circular door handle: The cross product shows how the angle of the squirrel's push (force vector) relative to the handle (position vector) determines how fast the door swings.

section_5.title: Summary & Quick Recall (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: 2D gives area (scalar), 3D gives a perpendicular vector. Emphasize: The Right-Hand Rule is the 'North Star' for direction.
section_5.example: A quick interactive flash-test: Show two vectors in 3D space; ask the student to point their thumb in the direction of the cross product.

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Algebraic Mechanic: Determinant Method", 
                          ["Use 3x3 determinant with unit vectors.", 
                           "Expand using minor 2x2 determinants.", 
                           "Calculate i, j, and k components."])
        
        # Matrix Setup
        matrix_str = r"""
        \begin{vmatrix}
        \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\
        a_x & a_y & a_z \\
        b_x & b_y & b_z
        \end{vmatrix}
        """
        matrix = MathTex(matrix_str, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Minor determinants
        minor1 = MathTex(r"\mathbf{i} \begin{vmatrix} a_y & a_z \\ b_y & b_z \end{vmatrix}", color=BLUE)
        minor2 = MathTex(r"-\mathbf{j} \begin{vmatrix} a_x & a_z \\ b_x & b_z \end{vmatrix}", color=GREEN)
        minor3 = MathTex(r"+\mathbf{k} \begin{vmatrix} a_x & a_y \\ b_x & b_y \end{vmatrix}", color=RED)
        
        minors = VGroup(minor1, minor2, minor3).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(minors, 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(minors))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        result = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = (a_y b_z - a_z b_y)\mathbf{i} - (a_x b_z - a_z b_x)\mathbf{j} + (a_x b_y - a_y b_x)\mathbf{k}", font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'F3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)
